chunks: Al-Ayyashi from Hamdawayh from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Sama'ah who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man whom the polytheists capture, and prayer time arrives for him, and he fears they will prevent him [from praying fully], so he gestures with a nod; he said, 'He gestures with a nod.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.إِيمَاءٌ: Gesturing (with head or body) as a substitute for full physical movements in prayer
key_terms.يَخَافُ: He fears (that they will prevent him)

ai.seo_question: How should a prisoner perform prayer if they cannot stand or bow due to their captors?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* and traced through the reliable chain of Sama'a, this hadith establishes the principle of *khawf* (fear of harm) as a valid excuse for modifying the physical postures of prayer. The Imam’s concise confirmation that gesturing suffices underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on flexibility (*rukhas*) when a believer faces external coercion, ensuring the obligation is met despite physical constraints.
